topic: Decoupling of Compute vs Decoupling Failure
value_1: Global data centre energy use was estimated at ~205 TWh in 2018 (representing a 6% increase from 2010 despite a 550% increase in compute instances) (pdf p. 2, ROW-0010, ROW-0011).
value_2: US data centre electricity consumption surged 131% from 76 TWh in 2018 (1.9% of US power) to 176 TWh in 2023 (4.4% of US power), and is projected to reach 325 to 580 TWh by 2028 (6.7% to 12.0% of US power) (pdf p. 7, 8, ROW-0020, ROW-0021, ROW-0023, ROW-0025).
locator_2: pdf p. 7, ROW-0021; pdf p. 8, ROW-0023
driver_of_divergence_I: Methodological vintage and architectural regime shift [I]. E01 analyzed the virtualization and hyperscale consolidation era (2010-2018). E02 captured the post-2018 explosion of GPU-accelerated computing and generative AI workloads where server wattage increased from ~500W to 10-40 kW per rack.
justification_sources_checked: Cross-checked across E01, E02, E03, E04, E05
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Strong empirical rigor in both; divergence reflects genuine historical transition [I]

topic: Data Centre Share of National Electricity Consumption
value_1: Data centres are projected to represent 2.6% to 3.3% of India's electricity consumption by 2030 (E09 pdf p. 14, ROW-0149), with AI data centres adding 26.3 GW of peak load by FY 2031-32 (~6.78% of 388 GW peak) (E11_P pdf p. 1, 3, ROW-0170, ROW-0174).
locator_1: pdf p. 14, ROW-0149; pdf p. 1, ROW-0170
value_2: Data centres consumed 7,663 GWh or 23% of total national metered electricity in 2025, exceeding the 18% share consumed by all urban residential dwellings (E16 pdf p. 1, ROW-0175, ROW-0176, ROW-0178).
driver_of_divergence_I: Economic scale and geographic denominator divergence [I]. Ireland possesses a small national grid (~33 TWh total) hosting massive European hyperscale headquarters. India possesses a continental grid (~1,600+ TWh) with massive agricultural, industrial, and railway baseloads, diluting national percentage shares despite huge absolute gigawatt additions.
justification_sources_checked: Cross-checked across E08, E09, E11_P, E16, E17, E19
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Robust official statistics in both; highlights that national share metrics cannot be directly compared without contextualizing grid denominator [I]

topic: Interconnection Queue Capacity vs Utility Metered Planning
value_1: Dominion Energy's contracted data center connection pipeline reached 53.8 GW in July 2026 across its service territory, as reported by a secondary trade source (pdf p. 2, WEB-0022).
value_2: Dominion plans and builds transmission to serve 1,000 MW of forecasted metered load even when data centre customers request 2,000 MW of capacity (pdf p. 69, ROW-0101).
driver_of_divergence_I: Contractual multi-queuing and speculative developer behavior [I]. Developers submit identical multi-hundred-megawatt applications across adjacent substations to secure priority, inflating paper queues 2x-3x above physical transformer delivery capacity.
justification_sources_checked: Cross-checked across E02, E06, E07, E13, E14, E15
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Queue figures are highly speculative; legislative audit and utility metered load data provide much higher empirical validity [I]

topic: Absence of Dynamic Load Models for Indian Power Grids
value_1: GRID-INDIA and SLDCs lack validated dynamic simulation models representing data centre electrical load response during grid faults or frequency sags (pdf p. 10, ROW-0157).
driver_of_divergence_I: Indian transmission planning models data centres as static P-Q bus loads rather than dynamic electronic converter loads with UPS fault ride-through thresholds [I].
justification_sources_checked: E08, E09, E11_P, E12 checked thoroughly; none contain empirical dynamic simulation parameters
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: High priority research gap for Indian grid stability [I]

topic: Corporate Non-Disaggregation of AI vs General Cloud Workloads
value_1: Google stopped disclosing machine learning energy share after 2021 (E04 pdf p. 1, ROW-0057), and operators refuse to disclose facility-level power or water metrics, masking AI consumption (E05 pdf p. 10, ROW-0083).
locator_1: pdf p. 1, ROW-0057; pdf p. 10, ROW-0083
driver_of_divergence_I: Commercial confidentiality and competitive posturing around proprietary AI model training efficiencies [I].
justification_sources_checked: E01, E02, E03, E04, E05 checked; all confirm lack of direct corporate disaggregation
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Forces researchers to rely on upstream silicon packaging proxies (TSMC CoWoS) [I]

topic: Econometric Ratepayer Bill Impact Modeling for Indian States
value_1: E3 and JLARC provide granular production-cost models showing Dominion residential customer bills could increase by $14 to $37 monthly by 2040 (E06 pdf p. 9, ROW-0091; E07 pdf p. 19, ROW-0109). No comparable cost-of-service studies exist for Indian states [I].
locator_1: pdf p. 9, ROW-0091; pdf p. 19, ROW-0109
driver_of_divergence_I: Absence of published cost-of-service studies by state electricity regulatory commissions (MERC, APERC, TSERC, TNERC) evaluating data centre infrastructure cost allocation [I].
justification_sources_checked: E08, E09, E11_P, E12 checked; Indian literature discusses discom revenue erosion qualitatively but reports zero econometric bill impact numbers
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Critical gap for dissertation research on Indian state equity [I]

topic: Secondary Press Reporting on CEA Advisory to States
value_1: E12 reports that the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) issued an advisory warning Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Tamil Nadu against grid tripping caused by data centre load surges (pdf p. 1, WEB-0009, WEB-0010).
locator_2: Ministry of Power parliamentary answer provides official national AI data centre projections (26.3 GW by FY32) (pdf p. 1, ROW-0170), but state-level advisories are not included in the attached record.
driver_of_divergence_I: ThePrint provides valuable ground reporting but does not publish the primary CEA advisory letters verbatim [I].
justification_sources_checked: Secondary dependency [I]. ThePrint provides reporting on the CEA advisory (pdf p. 1, WEB-0009, WEB-0010). However, the primary text of the CEA advisory letter is not included in the attached files; only the parliamentary answer on national projections (E11_P pdf p. 1, ROW-0170) is available as an official government document [I].
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Secondary journalistic framing; must be triangulated with official parliamentary filings [I]

topic: Corporate Market-Based Renewable Energy Scope-2 Accounting
value_1: Global data centre electricity implied carbon intensity was 395.65 gCO2/kWh in 2024 (E05 pdf p. 2, ROW-0077), while corporate sustainability reporting allows tech firms to use market-based Scope-2 accounting where Meta claims 98% clean energy through annual PPAs (E05 pdf p. 5, ROW-0081).
locator_1: pdf p. 2, ROW-0077; pdf p. 5, ROW-0081
driver_of_divergence_I: Annual volumetric renewable energy matching masks hourly grid carbon intensity and reliance on fossil backup during renewable lulls [I].
justification_sources_checked: Accounting construct vs physical reality [I]. Annual volumetric renewable matching does not ensure 24/7 hourly clean energy supply, masking local grid emissions and reliance on physical fossil-fueled baseload during renewable lulls [I].
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Weakest empirical indicator of actual grid decarbonization [I]

topic: Contracted Interconnection Queues vs Operational Metered Demand
value_1: Primary source E02 notes tracking interconnection queues risks overestimation due to projects applying in multiple utility queues (pdf p. 8, ROW-0029). Primary source E06 notes Dominion plans transmission to serve 1,000 MW metered load when customers request 2,000 MW capacity (pdf p. 69, ROW-0101). Secondary trade press source E15 reports Dominion's contracted queue reached 53.8 GW in July 2026, labelled as reported by a secondary source (pdf p. 2, WEB-0022).
locator_1: pdf p. 8, ROW-0029; pdf p. 69, ROW-0101; pdf p. 2, WEB-0022
driver_of_divergence_I: pdf p. 8, ROW-0029; pdf p. 69, ROW-0101; pdf p. 2, WEB-0022
justification_sources_checked: Paper queue distortion [I]. Interconnection queue numbers overestimate physical demand due to duplicate applications across utility service areas. Trade press numbers (53.8 GW) reflect speculative paper pipeline rather than committed construction [I].
weakest_evidence_assessment_I: Should never be cited as anticipated real electrical demand without severe haircuts [I]
